title: Am I running on opinion?
line: Five days of catching your views as they speak.
intro: Athena places opinion, δόξα, in the deep cave: most people, Athena says with Plato, run through the wonder-worker, “I have a view and I believe it”. For five days, catch your views as they come and ask what they rest on, which is where, in Athena’s words, one begins to leave the cave.
does: Three times a day, stop at a view you hold and ask what it rests on.
trains: Telling apart what you know from what you simply believe.
each: Three times today, when you hear yourself state a view (about a person, the news, politics, how things should be), stop and ask: am I conjecturing, or holding a view I simply believe? Then ask what it is based on: something I saw and tested, or something I was told, read or feel? No verdicts, only seeing.
note: One view you caught today, and what it was really based on.
end: Of all the views you caught, which did you hold most tightly, and what feeling was guarding it? Athena calls a conviction an opinion clothed in emotion.
later: Claude could read the five days’ views together and point out the patterns in them.
